articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a staggering 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw dubbed 'BlueHammer' — because apparently someone at Redmond decided April was the perfect time for a vulnerability fire sale.

articles.title: Google says criminals used AI to build a working zero-day exploit for the first time
articles.summary: Google confirms criminals used AI to craft their first working zero-day exploit, marking the official dawn of the 'Oh Shit, Skynet Learned to Hack' era. The future is here and it's debugging itself into our networks.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas platform gets pwned by extortion crew, disrupting education nationwide with ransom demands plastered on login pages. Nothing says 'back to school' like having your homework held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: Apple, Google drag cross-platform texting into the encrypted age
articles.summary: TanStack npm packages get poisoned in a six-minute supply chain blitz that pushed 84 malicious versions with credential theft and disk-wiping payloads. Speed-running software sabotage like it's a damn esports event.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches — peak hypocrisy from an administration that treats transparency like kryptonite.

articles.title: EFF to Fourth Circuit: Electronic Device Searches at the Border Require a Warrant
articles.summary: Canada repackages last year's surveillance nightmare as Bill C-22, proving that bad digital rights legislation never truly dies — it just gets a fresh coat of 'lawful access' paint.

articles.title: EFF Stands in Solidarity With RightsCon and the Global Digital Rights Community
articles.summary: EFF fights the Fourth Circuit for warrant requirements on border device searches, because apparently the Constitution gets confused at customs checkpoints.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after orchestrating SMS phishing campaigns. Another reminder that even elite cybercrime groups eventually meet their match in good old-fashioned law enforcement.

articles.title: Hackers Use AI for Exploit Development, Attack Automation
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' privilege escalation vulnerability threatens enterprise Linux distros, joining the hall of fame alongside Copy Fail and Dirty Pipe. Linux keeps finding creative new ways to hand out root access like party favors.

articles.title: How Open Source Dependency and Repo Attacks Compromise DevOps Pipelines and How to Stay Safe
articles.summary: Nine-year-old 'Dirty Frag' vulnerability enables root access on Linux systems with public PoC code now available. Because nothing says 'enterprise security' like decade-old privilege escalation bugs finally getting their moment to shine.
